bio: Toronto-born Punjabi-Canadian rapper and singer Sunny Malton is a major figure in modern Punjabi hip-hop, known for his work with Sidhu Moose Wala and the Brown Boys collective.

Sunshine Makers are a psychedelic soul-funk collective that began as a Toronto project in 2017 before taking root in London, Ontario. Led by songwriter Brent Jackson, the group blends R&B, funk, jazz and neo-soul with lush vocal arrangements and an uplifting focus on love, unity and community.
Winnipeg art-rap ensemble Super Duty Tough Work recreates the dusty jazz-sample feel of 1990s East Coast hip-hop with a live band, politically charged writing and meticulously arranged performances.

Inuk singer-songwriter Susan Aglukark blends Inuit musical traditions with pop and country songwriting, becoming a groundbreaking Canadian recording artist and the first Inuk performer to win a Juno Award.
Mississauga-born singer-songwriter Suzie McNeil is a Canadian pop-rock vocalist and multi-instrumentalist whose solo career followed national exposure on Rock Star: INXS.
Toronto hip-hop trio Swamp Thing brings together Timbuktu, Chokeules and Savilion for dark, B-movie-inspired underground rap built around boom-bap production and horror and sci-fi imagery.

Vancouver hip-hop group Swollen Members emerged at the end of the 1990s around rappers Madchild and Prevail, with producer Rob the Viking becoming central to the group's sound and Moka Only contributing during key early years. Their 1999 debut Balance connected the West Coast Canadian underground to a wider North American rap network through collaborations with artists including Dilated Peoples, while establishing a dense, battle-informed style that sounded distinct from the Toronto scenes then dominating the national conversation.

The group broke much wider with Bad Dreams in 2001 and Monsters in the Closet in 2002. Songs such as "Fuel Injected" helped turn Swollen Members into one of the most visible Canadian rap acts of the early 2000s, and the JUNO Awards later highlighted their four Rap Recording of the Year wins in 2001, 2002, 2003 and 2007 as evidence that Canadian hip-hop was gaining major traction beyond Toronto. Albums including Black Magic and Armed to the Teeth kept the group active through lineup changes, commercial shifts and periods of instability.

Swollen Members continued recording into the 2010s with Beautiful Death Machine and Brand New Day before the core trio spent several years apart. Their 2024 reunion for Vancouver's SwollenFest and a 17-city Canadian tour returned Madchild, Prevail and Rob the Viking to the stage together. The group's larger Canadian significance lies in geography as much as longevity: they helped make Vancouver a nationally visible hip-hop centre and demonstrated that a commercially viable Canadian rap identity could develop outside the country's dominant Toronto pipeline.
Québec singer-songwriter Sylvain Cossette is a long-running French-Canadian pop and rock artist whose solo career followed his years with the English-language band Paradox.

Toronto producer T.R.A.C.K.S. is a Canadian hip-hop beatmaker and former member of IRS and the Monolith collective whose production work helped shape Scarborough's late-1990s and early-2000s rap scene.

Toronto producer T.R.A.C.K.S. is a Canadian hip-hop beatmaker and former member of IRS and the Monolith collective whose production work helped shape Scarborough's late-1990s and early-2000s rap scene.

TAAYLEE G is a Toronto rapper whose music blends sharp, confident bars with melodic delivery and Caribbean influence. She emerged in the early 2020s, performed at Toronto's first Rolling Loud festival and later appeared on the 2023 Legacy Awards honouring Canadian hip-hop pioneers. Her feature on Golde London's 2025 Think They Know Me remix is her Northern Dial library credit.
Halifax rapper Tachichi is a veteran of Canadian underground hip-hop whose solo catalogue and collective work connect him to the long-running Backburner scene.
Toronto singer-songwriter and producer Tafari Anthony is a Canadian R&B and pop artist whose Juno-nominated work centers queer identity, emotional honesty and a wide vocal range.
Lévis duo Taktika is a foundational Québec hip-hop group whose decades-long French-language catalogue has helped define and popularize rap québécois.
Winnipeg-born singer-songwriter and guitarist Tal Bachman is a Canadian pop-rock artist best known for the international 1999 hit She's So High.

Toronto-born singer-songwriter Tallulah Argue is a Canadian artist whose music combines country, alternative pop and grungy Americana with witty, narrative-driven writing. After beginning her career in Toronto, she relocated to London to study and develop her work, releasing songs including Moonshine and the 2026 EP Deer in the Headlights.

Windsor, Ontario-born singer-songwriter Tamia entered the international R&B conversation before she had even released a solo album. After attracting the attention of Quincy Jones, she appeared on his 1995 album Q's Jook Joint, singing "You Put a Move on My Heart" and joining Babyface on "Slow Jams." Those performances helped earn her early Grammy recognition and established a voice defined by control, warmth and a strong connection to classic soul even as 1990s R&B production was becoming increasingly modern. Her self-titled 1998 debut then gave that voice a full album context, with "So Into You" becoming one of the decade's enduring slow jams.

Tamia expanded that audience through A Nu Day, More and Between Friends, balancing polished mainstream R&B with the kind of vocal-first songwriting that aged well beyond a single radio cycle. "Stranger in My House" became one of her biggest crossover records, while "Officially Missing You" and her collaboration with Eric Benét on "Spend My Life with You" further established her as a singer equally comfortable with intimate ballads and larger adult-R&B productions. Later albums including Beautiful Surprise, Love Life and Passion Like Fire extended her catalogue without forcing her into trend-chasing reinventions.

Her significance to Canadian music is easy to miss because so much of her commercial career unfolded inside the U.S. R&B industry, but that is precisely why it matters. Tamia was one of the clearest examples of a Canadian-born Black vocalist sustaining a long international R&B career before Toronto became globally synonymous with the genre. Across six Grammy nominations and decades of recording, she helped demonstrate that Canadian R&B could travel without losing the vocal traditions that shaped it.

Scarborough rapper and R&B artist Tamir Holder is a Canadian MC whose music combines agile rap flows with melodic vocals and writing about Scarborough, love, Black identity, masculinity and mental health. He has built an independent catalogue including Don't Let Your Fear Kill You and later singles, and joined Kardinal Offishall, Tona, Scotty IV, Eternia, Quake Matthews and Promise on One For All (Remix).

Inuk artist Tanya Tagaq, from Ikaluktutiak (Cambridge Bay), Nunavut, transformed a tradition normally practiced by two singers into a fiercely individual improvisational language. She began experimenting with throat singing after leaving home for high school in Yellowknife, then developed a solo approach while studying visual art in Nova Scotia. Collaborations with artists including Björk and the Kronos Quartet brought that voice into international experimental-music settings, but Tagaq's work has never treated Inuit sound as a texture to be placed inside somebody else's framework. Her performances use breath, growls, cries, melody and physical improvisation to create music that can feel as close to free jazz, metal and contemporary composition as to conventional song form.

The 2014 album Animism became a national breakthrough when it won the Polaris Music Prize, with the jury recognizing a record that refused to soften either its sound or its politics. Retribution followed in 2016 with an even more explicit focus on colonial violence, environmental destruction and bodily autonomy. Tagaq later extended the same creative world into literature with the genre-blurring book Split Tooth, longlisted for the 2018 Scotiabank Giller Prize and winner of the 2019 Indigenous Voices Award for Published Prose in English. On 2022's Tongues, produced by Saul Williams, passages drawn from Split Tooth were set against industrial and electronic production, making the relationship between her writing and music especially direct.

Tagaq's 2026 album Saputjiji pushed that language into ambient, electronic and filmic sound design while confronting militarism, colonial systems and economic power. Across music, writing, visual art and performance, she has become one of the most internationally visible contemporary Inuk artists in Canada without reducing Inuit identity to heritage presentation. Her 2014 Polaris win, 2015 JUNO for Aboriginal Recording of the Year and 2016 appointment as a Member of the Order of Canada reflect the institutional recognition, but her larger importance lies in how forcefully she has expanded the space available to Indigenous experimental art on major Canadian and international stages.
Montréal-born rapper Tara Chase is a pioneering Canadian female MC who became part of Toronto's influential Circle collective and helped establish women in Canadian hip-hop during the 1990s.

Edmonton MC, DJ and producer TARiiiQ, born Tariq Bakir, built his music around the traditions of conscious hip-hop while keeping the production palette deliberately open. Originally from Palestine and based in Edmonton, he first developed as a DJ before moving deeper into rapping and production, drawing on boom-bap, jazz textures and the foundational language of hip-hop.

Since beginning his recording catalogue in 2019, TARiiiQ has expanded beyond traditionalist rap into trap, downtempo, lo-fi and psychedelic production. His 2024 full-length work and subsequent releases helped push his catalogue past half a million collective streams, while performances with a full band have taken him to venues and festivals including Edmonton’s Starlite Room, North Country Fair, JazzFest, Starbelly Jam and Shambhala.

Activism is central to his writing rather than an occasional theme. TARiiiQ has used hip-hop to address occupation, violence and Palestinian identity while also celebrating culture and community. Within Canadian rap, that gives his work a distinct role: he connects Edmonton’s independent scene to a wider political hip-hop tradition and treats production versatility as a vehicle for message rather than a substitute for it.
Toronto DJ Tasha Rozez is a Canadian reggae and dancehall selector and soundsystem figure known as Gunz'n'Rozez and recognized as a pioneering woman in sound-clash culture.

Tassja is a Canadian singer associated with Toronto and Halifax hip-hop and R&B circles. Her catalogue includes the 2006 Spesh K collaboration 'Retirement Days,' while she later appeared in Drake's 'Started From the Bottom' video and pursued her own music as Tassja Dawn. Northern Dial carries Tassja as part of its Canadian R&B and hip-hop catalogue.

Calgary-born singer-songwriter and dancer Tate McRae first built an audience through dance and self-released music online before the 2020 single "you broke me first" turned her into an international pop breakout. Her debut album i used to think i could fly kept much of that early confessional tone, framing heartbreak and insecurity in sparse, digitally native pop while her background as a high-level dancer remained a separate but increasingly important part of her performance identity.

McRae's second album THINK LATER marked a much bigger pop turn. The global hit "greedy" paired a harder rhythmic sound with choreography-forward visuals and helped move her from singer-songwriter breakout to arena-scale pop performer. At the 2024 JUNO Awards, "greedy" won Single of the Year and McRae won Artist of the Year. The following year, THINK LATER won both Album of the Year and Pop Album of the Year, "exes" won Single of the Year and McRae repeated as Artist of the Year.

That momentum accelerated with 2025's So Close To What, which became her first No. 1 album in both Canada and the United States. The record broadened her 2000s-informed pop palette through dance-pop, Miami bass and other club-oriented textures while putting her choreography more centrally into the way the songs were presented. By 2026, after another run of major chart records and her first GRAMMY nomination, McRae had become one of the clearest examples of a new Canadian pop generation in which songwriting, short-form discovery, high-level dance and large-scale visual performance are parts of the same career rather than separate lanes.

TAURO formed in Toronto from the unlikely but productive meeting of two different musical backgrounds: jazz pianist and singer-songwriter Cynthia Tauro and Brendan Canning, co-founder of Broken Social Scene. The pair met around Toronto's Field Trip festival in 2022 and began writing together soon afterward, using informal sessions to find common ground between Tauro's jazz training and Canning's long history in indie rock, electronic music and collaborative band culture. Their 2024 debut single "Great Minds" introduced a down-tempo sound drawing from alternative R&B, soul, trip-hop and keys-forward pop rather than trying to reproduce either member's established lane.

The project developed through singles including "You Got Something" and "Change Is Strange," with "Great Minds" reaching the CBC Music Top 20. TAURO's recordings have involved a wider Toronto network that includes musicians and producers connected to Jessie Reyez, Daniel Caesar, Sam Roberts Band and other parts of the city's contemporary music community. That collaborative structure is central to the project: the songs are built less around a fixed genre than around the interaction between Tauro's harmonic instincts and Canning's atmospheric, groove-oriented approach.

By 2026, TAURO had moved from a singles project into its first album-length statement, Act I. The record centres change, distance and emotional recalibration while keeping the project's blend of indie, soul, jazz, R&B and trip-hop deliberately fluid. TAURO matters within the current Toronto scene because it connects generations and networks that are often discussed separately: a younger jazz-rooted songwriter, a veteran of Canada's internationally influential indie-rock era and a circle of contemporary producers working across R&B and pop.

Taylor Jackson is a Winnipeg-based Canadian singer-songwriter whose music sits between indie rock and contemporary singer-songwriter pop. Her releases include the Boring EP and the 2025-26 singles I Lose My Mind and Buzzcut, with Manitoba community radio identifying her as both a local and Canadian artist.

Tecun B'alam is a Calgary-based Kaq'chikel hip-hop and R&B artist whose work connects Indigenous solidarity, political performance and contemporary rap. Identifying himself as the Mayan man on Treaty 7 land, he has built a catalogue including A Better Version Of Me, 4myBB and Red Music Vol.1; three tracks from Red Music Vol.1 appear in the Northern Dial library.
Haiti-born, Montréal-rooted singer-songwriter Tedy is a Canadian pop artist whose emotionally vulnerable songs grew from an early YouTube following into a Sony Music Canada recording career.

Tegan is a split library credit for Tegan Quin of the Canadian duo Tegan and Sara. Calgary-born twin sisters Tegan and Sara Quin built an internationally acclaimed career spanning indie rock, alternative pop and synth-pop, with records including The Con, Sainthood, Heartthrob and Love You to Death.
Weyburn, Saskatchewan singer-songwriter Tenille Arts is a Canadian country artist whose melodic, contemporary songwriting has produced platinum-certified singles and a growing international career.
Grande Prairie, Alberta singer-songwriter Tenille Townes is an award-winning Canadian country artist known for vivid storytelling, intimate vocals and self-produced, emotionally direct songwriting.
Vancouver-based artist Teon Gibbs blends R&B, soul and hip-hop with smooth vocals, relatable writing and community-building work through his 100 Collective platform.
Toronto producer, DJ and electronic artist Tep No is a Canadian musician known for low-key tropical-house and dance-pop built around restrained beats, guitar and breathy vocals.
Vancouver rapper Terell Safadi is a Canadian West Coast independent artist whose catalogue and touring career include collaborations with The Game, DJ Mustard, Tory Lanez and Pressa.

TESSA is the Canadian pop and R&B project built around Sudbury-born singer-songwriter Tessa Gooden and Toronto-based producer and multi-instrumentalist Petr Balaz. Their releases include the 2018 album Fool Love and singles such as Honesty, blending pop, R&B and soul production. Northern Dial carries TESSA as part of its Ontario independent pop catalogue.

The 45 Portland Street Band is a Dartmouth, Nova Scotia studio collective assembled from artists connected to the creative community around 45 Portland Street and Fang Recording. The project appeared on the 2025 Joel Plaskett tribute Songs From The Gang with Drunk Teenagers, featuring Eric Stephen Martin, Alexander Gallant, Aquakultre and Sarah Swire alongside Lance Sampson, Brendan Morley and Dylan Jewers.
Toronto rapper The 6th Letter, born Kevon André Samuels, is a Canadian MC associated with the Bakers Club collective and Toronto's early-2010s underground rap wave.
Regina-rooted band The Age of Electric was a Canadian alternative-rock group whose melodic 1990s catalogue helped launch the later careers of members Ryan Dahle, Kurt Dahle and Todd Kerns.
Montréal-formed The Barr Brothers is a Canadian-American indie-folk band whose layered sound combines Americana, blues, harp, experimental textures and roots songwriting.

The BLK LT$ is the musical project of Toronto-born singer, songwriter and producer Andreena Miller. Known earlier as Andreena Mill, she has earned Juno nominations, collaborated with artists and producers across hip-hop and R&B and developed a catalogue that moves between soul, R&B and hip-hop production.
Toronto production group The Boomtang Boys is a Canadian dance and electronic act known for remix work and late-1990s pop-dance hits including Squeeze Toy and Movin' On.

Vancouver producer, vocalist, DJ and educator the della kit, born Dee Landsberg, is a Canadian R&B, soul and jazz artist whose work combines live musicianship, experimental production and sound-healing practice.
Toronto duo Dream Warriors is a pioneering Canadian hip-hop group whose jazz-sampled 1990 debut And Now the Legacy Begins became one of the country's first internationally successful rap albums.
Montréal collective The Foundation is a Canadian genre-blending ensemble led by Fredy V and Mel Pacifico, combining funk, R&B, Afrobeats and hip-hop with a rotating cast of musicians and producers.
Kingston rock band The Glorious Sons is a Juno-winning Canadian group known for anthemic songwriting, arena-sized performances and a modern take on hard-driving rock and roll.

HalfSizeGiants are an Ottawa hip-hop group formed by childhood friends Ironic, Memo Moreno and Jahiant, who grew up together in the city's south end. Originally known as B.M.W., the trio blended hip-hop with Jamaican and Latin influences, first making their mark in the 1990s before reuniting years later.

The Killjoys emerged from Hamilton, Ontario, in the early 1990s with a sound that pulled power pop and punk energy into the alternative-rock moment. Mike Trebilcock, Shelley Woods and Gene Champagne recorded their debut Starry independently in Hamilton, and songs such as "Dana" and "Today I Hate Everyone" helped the group move from regional attention to national exposure. Warner Music Canada picked up and reissued the album in 1994 after "Dana" gained strong CFNY support, while the blunt, hook-heavy "Today I Hate Everyone" became the band's signature MuchMusic-era single.

The 1996 follow-up Gimme Five pushed the band further into Canadian alternative radio. "Rave + Drool" appeared on the first Big Shiny Tunes compilation, while "Soaked" and other singles kept The Killjoys visible during a period when Canadian guitar music was moving rapidly between independent scenes and major-label rock. In 1997, the group won the JUNO Award for Best New Group. Melos Modos followed as their third studio album, extending the catalogue before the original run wound down near the end of the decade.

The Killjoys' importance is less about international scale than about how clearly they capture a particular Canadian 1990s ecosystem: Hamilton roots, CFNY and MuchMusic exposure, independent credibility, a Warner deal and songs built to survive the shift from grunge-era radio toward sharper power pop. The band later reunited for periodic shows and returned to Starry for a 30th-anniversary vinyl edition in 2024, adding new recordings to an album that had never originally been issued on vinyl. That continuing activity has kept the group's most durable songs connected to the scene that produced them rather than freezing The Killjoys as a one-era artifact.
Toronto producer and multi-instrumentalist The Kount is a Canadian beatmaker known for groove-heavy instrumental music that blends hip-hop, funk, jazz and contemporary R&B.
Canadian sibling band The Moffatts moved from country music into polished pop-rock and teen pop, building a major international following during the 1990s.
Trois-Rivières band The New Cities was a Canadian synth-pop and dance-rock group that blended pop-punk guitars with electronic production during the late 2000s and early 2010s.
